Subject: Implementation cadence and MAP for Verge Health deployment

Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Verge is excited to get started. Attached is the MAP we started (Verge_MAP_v1.xlsx) — it's a simple mutual action plan that combines rollout milestones, testing windows, and a training schedule. Can we confirm the high-level timeline so we can lock internal approvals and start procurement?

Key asks from our side:
- A two-week canary in production limited to 5% of traffic (non-PHI test dataset)
- An evaluation plan for quality regressions vs. our baseline (we'd like per-prompt pass/fail and a snapshot of embeddings drift)
- Training for our ops and application teams (up to 12 people), ideally in two 90-minute sessions plus an office hours week

I attached the MAP and an internal infra contact (infra@vergehealth.com) — please include them where relevant for networking and capacity checks.

Emma Li
Director, Product Operations
Verge Health

Emma — thanks, this is a helpful starting point. I pulled the MAP into a draft cadence and added canary/migration steps inline. High-level proposal below; see attached for a row-by-row MAP with owners.

Proposed high-level timeline (week numbers relative to signature):
- Week 0 (sign + account setup): provisioning, VPC peering checklist, assign Dedicated pool (if requested)
- Week 1: Integration & smoke tests; run a short synthetic load to validate KV cache behavior
- Week 2–3: Canary window (2 weeks). Start at 1% traffic for 48 hours, expand to 5% pending KPIs
- Week 4: Full migration ramp (25% -> 50% over 48 hours -> 100%) with rollback gates
- Week 5–6: Training + knowledge transfer (two 90-min sessions + office hours week)

Evaluation plan summary (attached Verge_EvalChecklist.pdf):
- Baseline metrics: generation latency p50/p95, per-prompt quality pass rate, embedding similarity drift
- Acceptance: 95% prompt pass rate on the acceptance set, no >10% increase in 95th percentile latency
- Regression handling: automated rollback on sustained quality drop + human review gate

Operational owners:
- Redwood infra/capacity: marissa.cole@redwood.com
- Redwood integration lead: laura.bennett@redwood.com
- Verge infra contact: infra@vergehealth.com

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the canary windows above and the attendee list for training.
2) If Verge wants reserved Dedicated capacity, we'll include the Dedicated pool commitment in the order form (we can outline cost delta).
3) I'll publish the MAP on Drive and link it in HubSpot (sharing link included below).

Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Karthik — quick notes from infra/ops perspective (looping in Marissa and Vivek to own capacity and runbooks):

- Dedicated capacity: Verge's canary at 5% with expected peak concurrency looks like it will need a small Dedicated pool during the canary to guarantee latency SLOs. Marissa, can you size a minimal pool for the two-week canary and the ramp periods?
- Network: Verge uses a private VPC with strict egress rules. We will need an IP allowlist and a short tunnel verification procedure (2–3 hours) during Week 0. Infra (infra@vergehealth.com) — please share a contact for NAT/peering testing.
- Rollback: define automated fallback to a lower-capacity, quantized variant if the eval check fails (we've done this elsewhere). Add this to the MAP as a named step so CS/ops can trigger it.

Evaluation specifics I recommend adding to the MAP:
- A 'smoke-check' suite that runs on new commits during the canary and again at ramp points (owner: laura.bennett@redwood.com)
- A daily quality digest in the first two weeks (email + dashboard snapshot) with highlight flags for any prompt that drops below the pass threshold

Finally, training: please include a proposed list of attendees (roles) rather than names — we can accommodate up to 12. We'll propose dates for two sessions the week after ramp confirmation.

-Laura

Adding the canary guard rails and monitoring checklist into the MAP now. A few specifics I'm putting into the MAP (and Verge_EvalChecklist.pdf):

Canary guard rails (technical):
- Start at 1% for 48 hours. If no critical alerts and quality >95% on acceptance set, expand to 5% for remainder of window.
- Keep KV cache warms pinned per session to avoid tokenization divergence during initial traffic.
- Sampling: capture 1 in 200 requests for manual review; capture embeddings for drift analysis daily.

KPIs to surface in the daily digest:
- Prompt pass rate (acceptance set)
- Latency p50/p95 and token rates
- Error rate (5xx / timeout) and infra alarms
- Embedding cosine drift summary vs. baseline snapshot

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Pass rate >=95% on acceptance set across canary week
- p95 latency not exceed baseline + 10%
- No recurring 5xx spikes or infra alarms for 2 consecutive cycles

I'll attach the EvalChecklist and put a tabbed timeline in the MAP with owners. Karthik — once Emma confirms attendee roles, I will draft the training agenda (session 1: ops & SRE; session 2: product & app dev).

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
